description: In kithd/src/peer_fetch.rs:466, the SHA-256 digest of a fetched blob is compared using string equality: if computed_hex != expected_sha256. SHA-256 used as an integrity hash (not a MAC) is not timing-sensitive in the same way an HMAC comparison is — an attacker who can guess the hash byte by byte gains nothing because they can compute their own SHA-256. However, it is a best-practice violation to use non-constant-time comparison for any security-derived value. Recommendation: use a constant-time comparison (e.g. subtle::ConstantTimeEq on the raw bytes, or ring::constant_time::verify_slices_are_equal) for defense in depth, even though the timing oracle here is not practically exploitable. Low priority but worth tracking as a hygiene item.
title: SHA-256 integrity check uses non-constant-time string comparison
